chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
Regarding a person in ihram who slaughters a bird, indeed upon him is the blood of a sheep, which he must pay; and if it is a chick, then a kid or a young lamb from the sheep.
And that which indicates that it is incumbent upon him to pay the value of the egg as one dirham when he is in ihram is what has been narrated:

key_terms.دَمَ شَاةٍ: The blood/value of a sheep (a standard unit of expiation)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration) for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation (fidya) for a pilgrim in ihram who kills a bird?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific fidya for slaughtering birds while in ihram, distinguishing between adult birds and chicks by assigning the value of a sheep or a young lamb respectively. It further establishes a fixed monetary penalty of one dirham for an egg, reflecting the juristic methodology of assigning tangible values to minor violations. This ruling is part of the broader chapter on expiation for errors and transgressions of ihram conditions, emphasizing the precision required in ritual purity and sacrifice.
